key_insight: GREx broadens referring-expression tasks from single-target only to realistic scenarios by supporting multi-target and no-target expressions and providing a unified evaluation framework across segmentation, comprehension, and generation.
problem_solved: Existing datasets and methods assume one expression maps to one object, which fails to capture multi-target and no-target cases needed for real-world referring expression systems.
method: Introduce a generalized benchmark (three new datasets/annotations) that include single-target, multi-target, and no-target expressions across segmentation, comprehension, and generation tasks.
Define a unified evaluation protocol and metrics that jointly assess RES, REC, and REG under multi-/no-target conditions.

Provide baseline models and evaluation scripts (or adapt existing vision–language models) to demonstrate how to handle multi-target grounding, no-target detection, and expression generation consistently.
impact: GREx enables more realistic training and evaluation of vision–language systems, pushing research toward robust, deployable referring-expression models that handle ambiguous, plural, or absent referents. Practitioners get benchmarked data, metrics, and baselines to build and compare generalized REx models.
visual_elements: Side-by-side image examples showing single-target vs multi-target vs no-target expressions (with overlays for ground-truth masks/boxes)
Pipeline diagram of a unified model handling RES/REC/REG with arrows showing shared representations and task-specific heads
Bar chart/table summarizing dataset statistics (counts of single/multi/no-target examples) and baseline performance across tasks
Metric schematic explaining the unified evaluation protocol (how matches, misses, and false-positives are counted for multi/no-target cases)
paper_title: GREx: Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation, Comprehension, and Generation
paper_authors: Henghui Ding, Chang Liu, Shuting He, Xudong Jiang, Yu-Gang Jiang
